sources.permafrost_share: Definition: radius 10 km = unpressurized LTV, walk back in < 5 h at 2 km/h, NASA EVA-EXP-0075 (NTRS 20200001071) p.22 & EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B (19/10/2020) §4.2.1.3.1 p.40 [TBR-EVA-EXP-0042-001]; depth 1 m = team choice (18/11/2026), result unchanged between 0.5 and 2 m; Polar Moon: computed by POLENTA (src/pipeline/ice_access.py, --step ice) from the LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0, column ice_depth (PDS Geosciences Node, urn:nasa:pds:lro_diviner_derived1:data_derived_prp; Paige et al. (2010) Science 330:479 DOI:10.1126/science.1187726), inside the USGS Artemis III regions, McClernan (2024) LGRS ACC 1 km grids DOI:10.5066/P1MEQ6UK. Landing points: Malapert 3654, Haworth 7259, Nobile Rim 1 3444. Site value = median over the landing points (team choice 19/11/2026: with the p10-p90 range an ice-free place got a full score for Malapert). p10-p90 spread: Malapert 0.007-0.666, Haworth 0.230-0.967, Nobile Rim 1 0.142-0.665. ISRU test: if the site has ice (> 0), Earth places without permafrost are excluded (tests.yaml, filtri_se_sito_positivo); Aristarchus: no cold traps for ice at 25 N, Hayne et al. (2021) Nature Astronomy 5:169 DOI:10.1038/s41550-020-1198-9 & Paige et al. (2010); Phoenix: ice at 5-18 cm at the site, Smith et al. (2009) Science 325:58 DOI:10.1126/science.1172339, mean depth 4.6 cm, Mellon et al. (2009) JGR 114:E00E07 DOI:10.1029/2009JE003417; Gale: at 4.6 S ice is not stable near the surface at equatorial latitudes, Mellon & Jakosky (1993) JGR 98(E2):3345 DOI:10.1029/92JE02355; the DAN WEH of 1.5-3.3 wt% is hydrogen in minerals, Mitrofanov et al. (2014) JGR Planets 119:1579 DOI:10.1002/2013JE004553; Mars: radius not defined by NASA (EVA-EXP-0042 §4.2.1.3.1.2: forward work), result independent of the radius (0 or 1 everywhere).
sources.subsurface_ice: Polar Moon (scenario B): LCROSS at Cabeus, Colaprete et al. (2010) DOI:10.1126/science.1186986, value to be confirmed for the shadowed areas of each site, while on the lit ridges at the site 0.2 ± 0.1 wt% (LRO LEND, Siegler et al. 2015 & Wueller et al. 2025 DOI:10.1029/2025JE009127 §6.1); Mars: Mars Odyssey GRS / Phoenix TEGA-SSI & Curiosity DAN/SAM, Boynton et al. (2002), Smith et al. (2009) DOI:10.1126/science.1172339 & Mitrofanov et al. (2014) DOI:10.1002/2013JE004553; Aristarchus: not ice (no cold traps at 25 N, Hayne et al. 2021 DOI:10.1038/s41550-020-1198-9) but indigenous water in the volcanic glass of the pyroclastic deposit: up to ~150 ppm (0.015 wt%) in large deposits and ~300-400 ppm (0.03-0.04 wt%) near vents, Milliken & Li (2017) Nature Geoscience 10:561 DOI:10.1038/ngeo2993 (abstract; Aristarchus value in their Fig. 3 not checked [NV]); 0.03 ± 0.02 wt% (100-500 ppm) is consistent with that range
